## Model Studio design + plan (2026-10-10) - YOUR REVIEW NEEDED
/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/: MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md (layers 1-4), 6 mockups (paint, cuboid/bone editor, car livery retexture, locked states, automatic library, AK-47 prompt flow), DESIGN-NOTES.md, 28 shots. Questions: plan placement (proposed: top "All models" plan); does "usable by anyone" in the library include "Use in project" (today's gate locks it); what happens to mods that use a removed library asset; real-weapon names (hold for review, not block); lawyer for ToS licence wording; budget for the paid AI-mesh quality test and a GPU worker; Hytale timing. Library eligibility gap closed in r2 (uploads, templates, derived content excluded). Blender headless proof of concept running -> I-blender-poc.md.
DECIDED 2026-10-10: Model Studio sits in the top "All models" plan (same tier as Texture Studio/Library). Server-side gate to follow when built.

## AI mesh / meshgen service (`feature/cyrus-r18-meshgen`, 2026-10-10)
Model Studio L4 as a flagged service: router (catalog -> template -> parts kit -> from-scratch script), cost estimate before running, node-2 sandboxed Blender worker on the job queue, checks, glb + manifest (`ai-generated-for-user`). All flags OFF, not wired into the build service, no migration. Report: `O-meshgen.md`; docs "Cyrus AI mesh (meshgen)".
1. **Pricing inputs (needed for any money figure):** set `cyrus_meshgen_price_input_per_mtok`, `..._output_per_mtok`, `..._cache_read_per_mtok` (USD per million tokens of the model you will use). Without them the UI can show tokens only. Then decide the customer price per asset: estimates are template ~5.7k tokens (measured 5.2-8k), kit ~11.6k (not measured), scratch ~19k (measured 15-20k), plus ~25 s of 4 CPU threads on node-2 per round, plus rejected rounds.
2. **Paid eval (budget decision):** 20+ real prompts per rung with a real model + vision look step, to measure success rate in <= 3 rounds and real tokens. Nothing here called a model.
3. **Isolated worker before rung 3 is ever on for customers:** the from-scratch rung runs model-written Python; the systemd sandbox held every PoC probe but a kernel escape is untested. Needs a microVM/gVisor worker (no network, no credentials). Rungs 1-2 run no model code and can use node-2 as is.
4. **GPU worker:** not needed for rungs 0-3 (Cycles CPU renders ~16-28 s). Only needed for faster previews (EEVEE) or image-to-3D (TRELLIS, MIT) later.
5. **Game budgets:** no shipped game declares `AssetProfile.meshBudget`; every real game is refused until its adapter sets one (FiveM/UE numbers need a person to check the engine docs). The flights used a made-up draft profile.
6. **Template roadmap (proposal):** next pistol/shotgun (rifle kit reuse), barrel/drum + lantern (kit already does them), furniture (table/chair/shelf), sci-fi panel/terminal, melee axe/hammer/mace (the sword excludes these words today), vehicle parts much later. Known weak: the rifle `drum` magazine reads like a wheel; the wooden crate's bands are thin.
7. Switch on order when ready: `CYRUS_MESHGEN=1` on the worker host only after the build-service wiring, the plan gate (Model Studio = "All models") and the catalog registration exist; `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH=1` only after item 3.

## Model Studio Layer 1: viewport + paint (`feature/cyrus-r16-viewport`, 2026-10-10)
Built behind flags, NOT deployed, NOT merged into a release. Docs: "Cyrus Model Studio: viewport and paint". Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/modelstudio-*.png`. The UI follows the v3 paint mockup, which you have NOT reviewed yet: please review the mockup and these shots together.
1. **Two settings, both off:** `cyrus_studios_enabled` (existing) AND the new `cyrus_model_studio_enabled`. Until both are on, only preview accounts see /studio/model. The new key is not in the admin settings catalog yet (add it there when you want a toggle in /admin).
2. **One new table** `CyrusModelDraft` (autosave drafts; no FKs). Needs the normal schema push at deploy, before the flag. Without it autosave answers "not available" (no 500s) and saving revisions still works.
3. **Plan gate as you decided:** paint/fill/decal/layers/drafts/save = "All models" only, server side, unknown plan = closed; view/orbit/previews/install/export never gated. Lower plans get the page in view-only.
4. **Finding to decide (guns):** the new grip_in_hand check shows today's Cyrus handgun defaults put the grip ~2/16 block from where vanilla holds tools in third person (3/16 in first person, 5/16 for the template's aiming state). Cause: the re-grip is computed under the gun's own rotation. Options: (a) re-grip to the vanilla fist (my recommendation, a small change in `lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts`, it changes shipped packs), (b) keep and verify on the real-client day. Either way: one Test Flight with a real client holding the pistol.
5. **Not built yet (next tasks):** compiling painted creature skins into the delivered BetterModel model (creature paint is saved as revisions only; item paint DOES ship, through the Texture Studio save); the production transport for the server preview renderer (it runs Chromium, so only on node-2; `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW=local` is refused in production); AI model candidates (the prompt dock is shown disabled); an entry link from the mod's Assets tab; ItemCuboidSpec 3D items (plan F3).
6. **Decisions taken here (change if you disagree):** half-transparent paint on items is snapped to solid/clear (Minecraft cutout); "Fill" defaults to the whole face (Same colour is an option); mirror reflects across the model's centre plane; layers per model max 16; a dev-only sample glTF crate appears in the model list only off production.

## Model Studio layer 2: cuboid + bone editor (`feature/cyrus-r17-editor`, worktree cyrus-r17, 2026-10-10) - NOT deployed, flag OFF
Our own editor (no Blockbench code). Docs: DOCUMENTATION.md "Cyrus Model Studio: cuboid and bone editor". Shots: /root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/editor-*.png (built from the v3 mockup you have NOT reviewed yet).
No migration, no table, no enum. One new OFF setting: `cyrus_model_editor_enabled` (page + API 404 while off).
1. **Review the editor shots** together with the v3 mockups (b editor). Layout, the read-only phone approve view and the AI candidate bar ("1 overlap", Apply part) are as mocked.
2. **Plan gate**: implemented as decided (All models; view/export never gated; unknown plan = view only). Saka sees the editor read-only. Confirm.
3. **Before turning it on** (in this order): (a) asset sync must keep editor saves when the mod is rebuilt (today the next build's generated creature would win, like textures had to be fixed); (b) RigSpec v1.1 + compiler rig-c2 (cube ids, UV pins, cube rotation) if you want those to ship: today they are editor-only and the validator says so; (c) a `CyrusModelDraft` table for server drafts (today drafts stay in the browser); (d) one real Test Flight: open, edit, save, rebuild, see the creature on a Paper 26.x server.
4. **AI edits**: the candidate + 3-way merge works against a deterministic fake only; the real backend (a change build returning a RigSpec) is not built and no model was called.
5. **Hytale exporter**: a DRAFT behind maturity "planned" (never shown to customers). Only 3 facts are verified (extensions + PNG, cuboids/quads + fixed materials, 64 px per block for mobs); 16 format guesses are listed as UNVERIFIED. It needs one real `.blockymodel` (from the official Blockbench Hytale plugin or a game file) to replace the guessed layout, and a Hytale client to test against, before it can move past "planned".
6. **Motion / effects (your decision 2026-10-10)**: the timeline core is game-neutral (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/timeline/`): typed track kinds (transform now; sound cue, particle, light, material, state machine declared as extension points), clip events at times, one deterministic sampler, a play/pause/scrub/loop/speed clock. Minecraft does not ship clip events yet (studio only).

## Motion core (feature/cyrus-r21-motion, 2026-10-10)
Built, tested, real-flown on node-2; NOT merged into feature/cyrus-r2's release, NOT deployed, behind CYRUS_DESIGNER (off). Plan: `cyrus-designs/v4-motion/MOTION-PLAN.md`; see it with `cyrus-research/motion-sheets/*.png` and `cyrus-designs/v4-motion/shots/`.
- **Decide gating** for motion / effects: option A (presets + effects on every paid plan, custom timeline editing at All), B (Saka+), or C (All). Until then the catalog v2 kinds `motion` / `effect` are not added.
- **Ability hook**: allow an item ability to fire a motion event (`trigger_motion`)? It changes the generated Ability class and every designer golden hash, so it needs a coordinated designer release.
- **Real-client test day** (standing tester): click a door and the pistol stand on 1.21.11 and 26.2; judge interpolation smoothness, the vanilla-particle stand-ins (muzzle flash = flame + crit + smoke), sound timing.
- **Confirm FiveM / RedM** as the first vehicle-capable target (wheels, seats, a player getting in); Minecraft will not build vehicles.
- **Studio shape**: own Motion tab (as in the mockups) or a timeline mode inside Model Studio?
- Note for the next Model Studio pass: the L1 viewport keeps its own `PlaybackClock` (lib/cyrus/modelstudio/clock.ts) beside the L2 editor clock; fold it into the editor clock so the studio has one clock.
- Merge order: feature/cyrus-r21-motion and feature/cyrus-r20-designers2 (bosses/HUD) both extend `gameplay/spec.ts` and `compile.ts`; whichever lands second resolves small, mechanical conflicts (kind lists, validation blocks).

## Config and Stats Studio (`feature/cyrus-r23-config`, worktree cyrus-r23, 2026-10-10) - NOT deployed, flag OFF
New OFF flag `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` (env; route + page + API + deliverConfig). No migration, no enum, no table (revision kind `config` and asset kind `config` are strings). Rebuild the build-service image (copies `configs.js` + generated `config-spec.js`). Real node-2 flights passed on Paper 1.21.11 and 26.2 (`config-flights-2026-10-10.json`). Docs: "Cyrus Config and Stats Studio". Report: `U-config-studio.md`. Decide:
1. **Plan gate:** proposed UNGATED on every plan (editing numbers is not asset creation; ownership/auth checked server side, fail closed).
2. **Billing:** values-only saves and deliveries call no model and cost 0 tokens. Confirm they stay free.
3. **"Just tweak a setting" recogniser** (`planConfigEdit`): wired only into the studio's "type it" box (no AI). Wiring it into the normal change-request path skips the model (changes billing, same open question as the designers' `planDesignEdit`). Approve or keep studio-only?
4. **Delivery:** `deliverConfig` exists (journal + rollback + reload/restart) but nothing enqueues it; the API answers 501 for "send to server" until the worker path for `CYRUS_DELIVERY` exists. Reload automatically after a save, or a "Deliver" click per change?
5. **Balance warnings** (template `safe` ranges are design judgement, not measurement): show to customers, or owner/admin first?
6. **Switch order:** `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO=1` on the web + build-service request side after the image rebuild; delivery after `CYRUS_DELIVERY`.
7. Phones are read only by design (confirm).

content.thinking:
I'm designing a unified "studio creature" function that merges the L1 paint and L2 editor geometry states into a single pure sync function, planning out its return shape covering both editor document and base state.

Working through the three-way merge logic across builds: tracing how a sequence of builds and editor saves should resolve when the base RigSpec changes versus stays the same, and whether an unchanged build (same spec hash as base) should just keep the editor doc as-is rather than triggering a new merge or recording a redundant spec row.

The fix needs to compute the merged spec, compile and deliver that, while still recording the generated RigSpec row with provenance marking it as superseded.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Now I'm defining a CreaturePaint type (texture size, encoded albedo layers, sha256, optional asset id) that gets stored alongside the creature so compileStoredCreatures can reproduce the paint later, with a size cap around 512KB to avoid bloating ModBuild results. I'm sketching a paint.ts module with helpers to extract paint from a paint document (only visible albedo layers, null if none) and to build a paintSkin function that recomposites the base raster -- throwing or passing through on size mismatch.

I'm working out the compositing logic: decode the layers, composite the albedo channel onto a copy of the base pixels, then snap alpha values (>=128 to 255, else 0), which correctly preserves transparency where the base was transparent and no paint exists. I need to make sure checkPaint validates stored paint via decodeLayers even though it's our own trusted data, and that compileStoredCreatures verifies the sha256 matches for determinism -- this shared path also covers the delivery module. # Cyrus Model Studio v3: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files (self-contained, no network): `viewport-paint.html` (a; `?mesh=1` = Layer 4 AI-mesh state), `model-editor.html` (b), `retexture.html` (c), `locked-states.html` (d; `?state=unknown|experimental`), `library.html` (e; `?tab=mine`), `prompt-flow.html` (f). Sources `src/` (v2 kit + `ms.css`, `ms.js`, `m3d.js`, `models.js`), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2, capped slice) → `shots/` (28 PNGs: dark, light and 390 px narrow for each). `ctl=0` hides the mockup bar.

## Principles
- **Same product as v2.** Shipped portal shell, Cyrus bar with a Texture / Sound / **Model** switch, glass panels, inspector tabs, prompt dock, narrow approve view.
- **Real geometry, not pictures.** `m3d.js` is a small deterministic canvas renderer standing in for three.js: orbit, picking, channel views, wireframe, affine-mapped textures. Painting writes real texels; the timeline scrubs a real pose; livery layer toggles rebuild every channel.
- **One accent.** Violet = selected/primary. Cyan = "now" (timeline playhead) only. Green/amber/red = pass/warn/fail. One exception: gizmo and axis triad use muted X/Y/Z red/green/blue, the 3D convention people expect.
- **Profile-aware truth.** Channels a game cannot ship are disabled with the reason (Minecraft Java item: albedo only). Delivery status per export target (FiveM "planned": the Windows worker is not built). Hytale shows its unverified format list. "Not run" is never a pass.
- **Legal class is visible.** Game-derived templates carry an amber badge, "kept for this session only, never shared", and ship delta-only. The library shows provenance, attribution and every check.

## Screens → data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| a Paint | `ItemCuboidSpec` draft of `glock_9mm` (9 elements, 22.5° grip), `TextureDoc` paint layer (51 px "worn edge"), `ItemModelSpec` contexts (6) + states (idle/aim/reload; reload slides the slide back), checks incl. `grip_in_hand` |
| a `?mesh=1` | L4 output: LOD0-3 vs `meshBudget` (sample numbers), materials as lossless channel layers, cleanup checks, provenance `ai-mesh` |
| b Editor | RigSpec `banshee` (8 bones, 12 cubes, 5 clips), live budgets vs real caps, box-UV net on the 128 sheet with Auto-pack / Pinned, candidate bar with "1 overlap" (3-way merge) |
| c Retexture | glTF template stand-in (8,788 tris, 7 slots), body_paint layers with albedo/rough/metal values, UV island view, export picker with delivery status, policy row from the adapter legal block |
| d Locked | `canAsset(plan, "model", "edit")` strings verbatim; plan matrix with the proposed rows marked; Hytale maturity flag |
| e Library | automatic contribution: states pending checks / in the library / held for review / removed / not shared; lib-1 filters; `libraryEligible` exclusions |
| f Prompt flow | "AK-47 with fire stickers" → L2 + L1 route → ItemCuboidSpec + decal layer → deterministic render (sha) + look check → hand fixes as revisions → library "held" (real-weapon name) |

## Component inventory (React)
`ModelViewport`, `ChannelSwitch`, `ToolRail`, `GizmoLayer`, `InGamePreview`, `UvTexturePanel`, `Outliner`, `BudgetPanel`, `TransformFields`, `UvBoxField`, `Timeline`, `CandidateBar`, `MaterialSlots`, `ChannelLayerList`, `UvIslandView`, `ExportTargets`, `LegalClassBadge`, `PolicyCard`, `PolyBudget`, `LibraryGrid`, `LibraryDetail`, `ContributionTable`, `LibraryStateBadge`, `PromptFlow`; reuse `StudioLock` and `PlanMatrix`.

## Interaction details
- Left drag on the model = tool (paint/select); right drag or empty space = orbit; wheel = zoom. B/E/G/I paint tools; Q/W/E/R/P select/move/rotate/resize/pivot; X mirror; Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z.
- Every stroke, drag, key or accepted candidate is one undo step; drafts autosave; "Save revision" is explicit.
- Narrow: turntable, what changed, checks, Approve / Reject; locked plans get view-only with no approve.

## Honesty notes
Sample content is labelled; poly counts, look-check scores and filter results are illustrative. The mockup renderer is not the production renderer (three.js) and the lantern proxy is lower-poly than its LOD1 readout. Gun display transforms, element rotation rules per version, everything Hytale, RAGE normal convention and every AI quality claim are unverified.

## Questions for the owner
1. **Plan:** Model Studio at All models (matches today's gate), or paint-only for Saka?
2. **Library access:** you said "usable by anyone"; the gate today treats "Use in project" as asset creation (All models for models). Open it to every plan, or keep browse-open / use-gated?
3. **Library removals:** when an asset is removed after a report, do mods already using it keep it?
4. **Real-weapon names** (AK-47, Glock): hold for review in the library (proposed) and allow freely in private mods?
5. **Terms of Service:** the automatic licence grant needs a lawyer's wording; also AI-output copyright per region. Who drafts it?
6. **Uploads gap:** `libraryEligible` lets user uploads through (`source: "user"`). Confirm they must be excluded (I think yes) so the code gets an `uploaded` source.
7. **L4 spend:** budget for the paid quality eval, a GPU worker, and Meshy/Tripo trials?
8. **Hytale:** build the emitter now behind the experimental flag, or wait for a real client to test against?
9. **Retexture templates:** session-only (proposed) is safest but means re-attaching the file each time. Acceptable?
10. Gizmo axis colours as the one accent exception: OK?

content.content:
## Cyrus Model Studio: viewport and paint

Branch `feature/cyrus-r16-viewport` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). Layer 1 of the Model Studio plan (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md`): a three.js viewport and paint-on-model for every model a project already holds. **Nothing is deployed and everything is flagged off.** The UI follows the v3 paint mockup (`viewport-paint.html`), which the owner has **not reviewed yet**. Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/modelstudio-*.png`.

### Gates (server side; the UI only shows the result)
- **Visibility** (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/access.ts modelStudioOpen`, `deps.ts modelStudioViewer`): the studios gate (a Cyrus user AND (preview account OR `cyrus_studios_enabled`)) AND (preview account OR the NEW setting **`cyrus_model_studio_enabled`**, default off, fails closed). Anyone else: 404 page / 404 API. The setting is read through the host seam (`getHost().settings`); it is not yet in the admin settings catalog (owner action).
- **Plan** (owner decision 2026-10-10: Model Studio sits in the top "All models" plan with Texture Studio / Texture Library). `lib/cyrus/engine-core/asset-gate.ts canModelStudio(plan, action)` maps every studio action onto the existing `canAsset(plan, "model", op)` (ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model = "all"): `view, orbit, preview` = keep, `install`, `export` are NEVER gated; `paint, fill, decal, layer, draft, save, ai_edit` = edit = top plan only. Unknown plan (lookup error, typo, future plan) fails closed for those and never for viewing; an unknown action is `bad_request`, never allowed. Lower plans open the same page in **view only** (orbit, channels, in-game contexts, previews) with the gate's reason and a link to the plans page. The Model Studio row is NOT added to the shared `PLAN_MATRIX` (it would leak a flagged-off product on the locked page); it is `MODEL_STUDIO_MATRIX_ROW`. `studioPlanView().edit.model` exists. Tests cover the whole plan x kind x op matrix plus every action x plan.

### What it paints (nothing invented)
| Model | Source | Geometry | Texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| creature | newest CyrusProjectAsset kind `model`, mime RigSpec (a build's creature) | RigSpec rest pose (`restMatrices` = creature preview's `poseMatrices`, tested equal), box-UV faces with the creature preview renderer's face corners | the compiler's skin (`layoutSkin` + `skinTextureSpec`, server side) |
| item3d | every item texture (block tiles excluded) + the mod's ItemModelSpec | extruded like vanilla item/generated (front, back, open edges per opaque texel) | the TextureDoc composite (spec + Texture Studio paint) |
| mesh | glTF 2.0 (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/gltf.ts`, bounded reader: GLB or embedded data URIs, no external URIs, caps 32 MB / 150k tris) | node transforms applied, TEXCOORD_0 | base colour image |
ItemCuboidSpec (3D cuboid guns, plan F3) does not exist yet; the mockup's 9-element glock is therefore an extruded item here. No project holds glTF meshes yet (L3/L4); a dev-only sample crate (`?model=sample_crate`, never in production) exercises the PBR lane.

### Pure core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/`, GPU-free, unit-tested)
- `math.ts` ray/triangle (two-sided Moller-Trumbore), barycentrics, UV -> texel (top-left origin, clamp or REPEAT), orbit camera ray (= the three.js PerspectiveCamera).
- `scene.ts` one triangle soup per model + per-face UV regions; `pick.ts` nearest hit (coplanar ties: the lower triangle, i.e. the cube defined first), mirror-X by reflecting the RAY (cube nets are not mirrored in UV space), UV islands (fill region for meshes), triangle rasteriser.
- `layers.ts` per-channel lossless layers (albedo, normal, roughness, metallic, emissive, mask), opacity + blend (normal, multiply, screen, add, overlay), integer maths, region recomposite; storage `rle1` (varint runs + RGBA, base64; an empty 2048^2 layer is a few chars).
- `paint.ts` ops in texel space: brush (square/round, 1-64), erase, fill (resolved spans: whole face / same colour), decal stamp (clip to the face), layer add/set/delete/move. Deterministic; symmetry resolved at input. Session = base + op log + cursor; undo/redo replay from cached checkpoints; one stroke/fill/stamp/layer change = one step; > 200 steps fold into the base. `checkOp` validates untrusted logs.
- `doc.ts` ModelDoc v1 (`application/vnd.cyrus.modeldoc+json`): `{v, kind, name, base (rigspec+spec | texture | gltf, by asset id + sha), tex, layers, symmetry, log {ops, folded, sha256}}`; `startLayers` = what client and server both start a session from.
- `channels.ts` profile-aware view modes Lit/Albedo/Normal/Rough/Metal/AO/Emissive/Mask: channels the game's asset profile cannot ship are disabled with the reason (Minecraft Java: albedo only; mask is an authoring aid; AO is baked at export, never painted).
- `minecraft/contexts.ts` (the Minecraft adapter; game-specific display logic stays out of the core, which only consumes the generic `rig.ts` ContextRig) display contexts studio/gui/ground/first person/third person/fixed/head/on_shelf from `itemmodel` `stateDisplays` (the pack's own numbers; `displayMatrix(t)` is tested equal to `applyDisplay` on every vanilla category and the gun). on_shelf: Cyrus and vanilla items write no transform, so identity (unverified). **grip_in_hand**: the fist is FIXED at the point where vanilla tools put their handle (`HAND_ANCHOR` = item/handheld applied to `TOOL_HANDLE`); the in-game preview draws the hand THERE, not on the item's grip (the old preview drew the fist on the grip, so a gun always looked held). Per category reference: gun = vanilla tool fist; bow/crossbow = vanilla's own hold of the sprite centre; others = their vanilla handle. Third person is the real check (pass <= 1.5/16 block, fail > 3/16); first person is advisory (vanilla draws no arm while an item is held).
- `merge.ts` the conflict rule: 3-way per layer id and per texel; disjoint changes merge, overlaps are counted, the human wins by default; "Apply part" = selected layers only; deleted-vs-changed is an overlap.
- **Scene-time hooks for animation and effects (owner decision 2026-10-10: motion/effects with live simulation are foundational and game-agnostic; not built here, only not blocked):** `clock.ts PlaybackClock` (play, pause, seek/scrub, loop, speed, range, current time; deterministic `tick(dt)`; the viewport ticks it from requestAnimationFrame while playing), `pose.ts` (`PoseProvider.poseAt(t, scene)` -> per-node (part) transform overrides, `evalPose` composes providers, `posedScene` bakes them so the pure pick stays exact on a posed or playing model, `overridesJson` for the server). Viewport (`model-viewport.ts`): one mesh per part, `clock`, `setPoseProviders`, `setPartOverrides`, `addOverlay/removeOverlay` (overlay layers such as particles or gizmos with `attach(three, group)` + `update(t)` driven by the clock), `posed()`, `renderAt(t)`. Server preview: `previewRequest(..., { time, overrides })` (time and overrides are in the cache key; the page applies the overrides per triangle), so live view and deterministic render agree at any t. A creature clip provider (from RigSpec clips) and effect providers are the next consumers.
- `budget.ts` the plan's numbers (60 fps <= 64 cubes, 150k tris, 4 x 2048^2 channels, 512 MB GPU, stroke-to-pixel 16 ms, phones < 760 px with DPR <= 1.5).

### Finding: the Cyrus handgun defaults miss the vanilla fist
Measured with grip_in_hand on today's defaults (`lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts displayFor`, used by the pack): the idle pistol's grip lands **1.948/16 block** from the fist in third person (warn) and 3.148/16 in first person (advisory); the template's aiming state 5.079/16 in first person. Cause: the re-grip is computed under the GUN rotation (`regrip(R(gun), g, TOOL_HANDLE)` makes the grip land where a tool handle would land under the gun's rotation), not at the vanilla fist. Not changed here (it changes shipped packs and is unverified in a client either way); a test pins the numbers. Owner action below.

### Client (`components/cyrus/studios/`)
- `ModelStudio.tsx` page body (models list, UV texture, layers; header with undo/redo, draft state, Save revision; viewport with tool rail B/E/G/I/D, mirror X, orbit O, Wire/UV overlays, camera presets, channel bar; palette + brush strip; prompt dock shown disabled: model candidates are not built; In game panel with contexts, states and grip status; Checks / Paint / History tabs). Phones: read-only orbit + What changed + Approve (saves the autosaved draft as a revision) / Reject (drops it). WebGL missing: the server preview PNG.

Picking never uses three.js: the pure pick on the same arrays.
- Painting writes the live layers immediately (region recomposite + texture upload), pushes one op per stroke; items rebuild their extruded mesh when the silhouette changes.
- Autosave: 5 s idle, at most 30 s, to the draft; reopening restores it ("Restored your autosaved draft", Discard).
- Save conflict (409 stale_head): fetch the newer version, 3-way merge with the human winning, show the overlap count, save again.
- Entry: `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/model?model=<key>`; the studio switch shows "Model" in Texture/Sound only when Model Studio is visible (`showModel`). Not linked from the Assets tab yet.

### Save path (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/service.ts`, `http.ts`, `/api/cyrus/models/v1`)
- `GET projects?root=` models + access + renderer; `POST projects/:p/models/:key/revisions {doc, baseAssetId, expectedHeadId, log?}`; `GET|PUT|DELETE .../draft`; `GET .../preview?preset=&size=&source=saved|draft&context=&state=` (PNG). Viewer -> rate limit -> validation -> gate -> service; body cap 9 MB.
- creature: a NEW revision kind `asset` (manifest = head + `assets/models/<key>.modeldoc.json`) + a ModelDoc row (kind `model`, origin `edited`, provenance `{generator: "cyrus-model-studio", doc, basedOn, rigAssetId, logVerified, delivered: false}`). **Compiling the paint into the delivered BetterModel skin is not built** (the save says so).
- item3d: the albedo composite becomes the item's TextureDoc (spec untouched, every differing texel = paint, half-transparent texels snapped for cutout with a warning) and goes through the Texture Studio's own `saveTexture` (quality bar, pack rebuild, revision), so it ships exactly like a Texture Studio edit; the layers ride in `provenance.modelStudio` and reopen when the pixels still match.
- Stale rules: item base row must be the current texture row; creature base must be the current RigSpec row and the current paint row; `expectedHeadId` -> 409.
- Op log: when the session started from the saved layers and nothing was folded, the server re-plays the log (<= 2000 ops) and refuses a save whose pixels differ (400 `log_mismatch`); otherwise `logVerified: null`.
- Drafts: NEW table **`CyrusModelDraft`** (projectId, ownerRef, assetKey, baseAssetId, baseHeadId, doc, timestamps; unique project+owner+key; no FKs). Missing table = 503 `drafts_unavailable`, never a 500. `CYRUS_MODEL_DRAFTS=memory` (non-production) keeps drafts in-process.

### Server preview render (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/preview/`)
Injected `PreviewRenderer` interface + `previewRequest` (geometry and channel maps as base64, textures capped at 1024) + cache key `sha256(request + renderer id + version)` (in-memory LRU; the `CyrusPreviewRender` table is plan F1). Implementation `playwright.ts`: one fresh headless Chromium per render via `launchServer` (hard kill at the end, 60 s timeout, V8 heap 512 MB, one renderer process, no /dev/shm), three.js on SwiftShader, DPR 1, no antialias, no tone mapping, one frame; **no network**: every request is intercepted, only the page and `three.module.js` + `three.core.js` from node_modules are served, everything else aborted, DNS mapped to nothing. `select.ts`: off unless `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW=local`, and refused when `NODE_ENV=production` (production web/worker run on the primary, which never runs Chromium); the node-2 job transport for production is not built. Creatures face north, so presets turn 180.

### Tests and runs
- RAN on node-2 (`devhost test`): `test/cyrus-modelstudio.test.ts` (math, display matrices vs applyDisplay, grip_in_hand incl. the gun numbers, creature golden: every visible texel centre of every banshee cube face picks exactly its skin texel (1154 exact, 1074 occluded, 4 on a plane two cubes share), item and glTF picks, hostile glTF, mirror, layers round trip and blend maths, ops/replay/undo/fold, merge, doc, channels, budget, sha256 vs node, the full gate matrix, service + HTTP with fakes). Stroke-to-pixel at 2048^2 (16 px round dab + region recomposite, CPU only, GPU upload not included): median under 1 ms.
- RAN on node-2: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-render.test.ts` with real Chromium + three.js on SwiftShader: 4 golden images (banshee three-quarter / back, pistol studio / third-person rig) in `test/fixtures/cyrus-modelstudio/`, ~0.4-1.3 s per render, the same input twice = 0 differing pixels, separate launches 0.000 % off. Regenerate: `UPDATE_MODELSTUDIO_GOLDEN=1` and look at every PNG.
- RAN: fixtures through the real Prisma store (`scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` then `scripts/cyrus/modelstudio-fixtures.ts`: creature + item saves, both logs verified) and Playwright screenshots against `devhost dev` (`scripts/cyrus/modelstudio-shots.mjs`).
- NOT RUN: any real Minecraft client (display transforms, grip, painted creature skins); production DB / migration; the node-2 preview job transport; GPU-memory and real-GPU frame-rate measurement (headless SwiftShader only); AI model candidates (no backend).
## Cyrus Model Studio: cuboid and bone editor (layer 2, 2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r17-editor`, NOT deployed, flag OFF)

Our OWN cuboid + bone editor for RigSpec creatures (plan: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md` sections 2-3, 6; mockup `model-editor.html`, NOT owner-reviewed yet). Blockbench is GPL-3: nothing of it is embedded, copied or read; the document model, ops, merge rule and renderer are written from scratch. Layer 1 (three.js viewport + paint) is a separate branch (`feature/cyrus-r16-viewport`, uncommitted when this landed), so the editor draws through a thin adapter with an internal GPU-free canvas renderer until that viewport merges.

### 1. Pure core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/`, client-safe, no GPU, no `node:` in the client graph)
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `doc.ts` | `ModelDoc` v1 (mime `application/vnd.cyrus.modeldoc+json`): bones (id, name, parent id, pivot, rotation, tag, hide/lock), cubes (id, bone, from/to = origin + size, editor-only rotation + pivot + label, inflate, material/shade/fadeTo, texture slot, UV pin, decals), clips (tracks of keys with ids, or waves), texture slots, an id counter `seq` (replay gives the same ids). Zod parser for untrusted docs (`checkModelDoc`, 256 KB cap). |
| `rigspec.ts` | `fromRigSpec(spec, { like })` / `toRigSpec(doc)`. `like` lines a RigSpec (an AI candidate) up with a base doc: bones by name, cubes by identical from/to/material then by position, keys by (clip, bone, channel, t). `toRigSpec` reports editor-only fields it drops (cube rotation, UV pins, extra texture slots). |
| `ops.ts` | The v1 operations (plan section 3): add bone/cube, delete (subtree + its tracks), duplicate, mirror X (`_l`/`_r`, also mirrors decals and animation tracks), move/rotate/resize/scale with snapping (1 unit = 1/16 block grid; angle snaps), reparent (cycle-safe), pivot, UV pin/auto, rename, hide/lock, group, material/shade/inflate/tag, palette, clips + keys (set/delete/move/ease, wave -> keys, loop seam kept), `replace` (an accepted AI merge or a restored draft = one step). Locked nodes refuse edits. Ops never mutate their input. |
| `history.ts` | Undo/redo as an OP LOG `{ base, entries, at }` with a per-step cache; `replay(base, ops)` rebuilds any step from the base (tested byte-equal to the cache); 200 steps max (older ones fold into the base). |
| `validate.ts` | Structured issues `{ code, severity, path, node?, message }`: structure (ids, one root, parents, cycles, orphans), names/paths (bone/clip/model names, safe `assets/...png` slot paths), the RigSpec caps (constants from `creature/spec.ts`), the target profile (`profiles.ts`), the UV layout, then the authoritative `checkRigSpec` on `toRigSpec(doc)` with errors mapped back to the bone/cube. Live budgets for the panel. |
| `uv.ts` | Box-UV layout: auto boxes use exactly the compiler's shelf packer (rig-c1; test: same rectangles as `layoutSkin`), pinned boxes are placed first and auto ones flow around them. Pins are editor-only until RigSpec v1.1 / rig-c2 (warning `uv_pin_editor_only`). |
| `pose.ts`, `scene.ts` | Deterministic sampler (= `compile.ts sampleTrack`, tested), bone/cube world matrices (= `preview.ts poseMatrices`, tested), posed scene faces, camera projection, picking, gizmo axis drag maths. |
| `merge.ts` | The AI-edit merge rule: 3-way per node id (bone, cube, key, clip, track, palette colour, meta), field by field; a cube's box (from/to/pivot) is ONE field. One side changed -> that side; both changed differently -> an OVERLAP, human wins by default, `resolve` picks Cyrus per overlap; `accept` = Apply part. Cyrus's new ids are renumbered past both counters; a clashing new bone name is renamed for Cyrus's side; nodes left hanging are dropped with a note. |
| `gate.ts` | `canModelEditor(plan, action)`; the action -> asset-op map is `MODEL_EDITOR_ACTION_OP` in `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` (view/export never gated; edit, autosave, save, approve, ai_edit = edit; create = create). Top plan only, unknown plan fails closed for edits. (Layer 1 adds its own `MODEL_STUDIO_OP` map in the same file; unify them when both are merged.) |
| `autosave.ts` | Schedule: 5 s after the last edit, at most 30 s after the first unsaved edit. |
| `fake-candidate.ts` | A deterministic stand-in for an AI edit (base revision's RigSpec -> edit -> checkRigSpec -> `fromRigSpec like`). Used by tests and by `?fakeCandidate=1` outside production. NO model call anywhere. |

### 1b. Timeline core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/timeline/`, GAME-NEUTRAL, owner decision 2026-10-10)
Motion, animation and effects are a foundational, game-agnostic part of Cyrus (walk cycles, gun cock/fire/reload, car doors + a character getting in, explosions, fire, water), playable live in the studios and tied to the texture and sound studios. The timeline core is therefore its own folder with no Minecraft/RigSpec assumptions (game specifics live in `rigspec.ts` and the exporters); a later Motion core (EffectSpec ...) builds on these types.
- `types.ts`: `Clip { name, length (seconds), loop, tracks, events? }`, keys/events at NORMALISED time `t` 0..1. Tracks carry a typed `kind`: `transform` (bone/node rotation, position, scale; keys or a seamless wave) is implemented and stored in ModelDoc v1; `sound_cue`, `particle`, `light`, `material`, `state` are declared extension points (`TRACK_KINDS` status `planned`: shapes fixed and sampled, not stored in ModelDoc v1, not exported). `ClipEvent { id, t, name, data? }` = clip metadata "events at times" (stored; ops `setEvent` / `deleteEvent`; merged per id; editor-only for RigSpec v1 with warning `clip_events_editor_only`).
- `sampler.ts`: ONE deterministic sampler: `sampleClip(clip, time)` -> node transforms, scalar channels, machine states; `firedBetween(clip, from, to)` -> every instant (events, cues, bursts, state changes) crossed, half-open and wrap-aware (float drift at a wrap cannot drop an instant). Transform maths == `creature/compile.ts sampleTrack` (tested on every fixture track); `pose.ts` uses it.
- `clock.ts`: the playback API a viewport or a live simulation drives: `clockInit / Load / Play / Pause / Toggle / Scrub / Speed (0.1-4x) / Loop`, `clockTick(clock, dt, clip)` -> new state + fired instants + wraps + ended. Pure (the host feeds elapsed seconds). The editor's play button, speed select and the "event <name>" flash run on it.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-timeline.test.ts`.

### 2. Exporters (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/export/`, server only)
Game-neutral `ModelExporter { id, game, target, formats, maturity, unverified, run(doc, ctx) }`; `runExport` refuses maturity `planned` unless `allowPlanned` (tests/devhost only). Export is never plan-gated.
- `minecraft-bbmodel` (beta): `toRigSpec` -> `checkReturnedCreature` (re-validate, rig-c1 compile, skin quality) -> the creature JSON, `.bbmodel`, skin PNG. Byte-identical to what a build writes (tested).
- `hytale-blockymodel-draft` (**planned**, never offered to customers): uses ONLY the VERIFIED facts of `N-hytale.md` (V1 `.blockymodel`/`.blockyanim` + PNG, V2 cuboids/quads only + fixed materials, V3 64 px per block for mobs/equipment, 32 for blocks: the skin is upscaled 4x). Every other choice is listed as UNVERIFIED (`HYTALE_UNVERIFIED`, U1-U16: JSON layout and key names, units, node origins, quaternion order, face names and mapping, textureLayout, inflate as stretch, glow as fullbright, folder layout/no manifest, .blockyanim layout and 60 fps frames, delta semantics, scale tracks dropped, max texture size, clip-name mapping, baked waves). A sidecar `cyrus-export.json` says `loadedByRealClient: false`. Golden: `test/fixtures/cyrus-modelstudio/banshee.hytale-draft.golden.json` (regenerate only on a deliberate change: `UPDATE_MODELSTUDIO_GOLDEN=1`).

### 3. Save path (`service.ts`, `http.ts`, `deps.ts`; routes under `/api/cyrus/assets/v1/model-editor`)
- A mod's model = the newest `CyrusProjectAsset` of kind `model` for its key: a build's RigSpec row (`RIG_SPEC_MIME`) is converted, an editor row (`MODEL_DOC_MIME`) is read as is.
- Save revision (`POST .../model-editor/:projectId/:key`): gate (server side, fail closed) -> ownership -> parse -> validate (errors = 422 with issues) -> `checkReturnedCreature` (compile + skin quality, 422 if it fails) -> `expectedHeadId` (409 `stale_head`) -> NEW revision kind `asset` (manifest: `assets/creatures/<name>.json`, `bettermodel/<key>.bbmodel`, `assets/models/<name>.modeldoc.json`) + a new asset row (origin `edited`, provenance = doc + explicit RigSpec + hashes). Drafts are cleared.
- Drafts (`PUT .../draft`): `DraftStore` interface; there is NO `CyrusModelDraft` table yet (plan task F1), so production answers 503 and the client keeps the draft in the browser (localStorage), offering Restore/Discard on reload. Devhost: `CYRUS_MODEL_EDITOR_DRAFTS=memory`.
- Export (`POST .../export`): maturity-gated, never plan-gated; planned exporters only with `CYRUS_MODEL_EDITOR_PLANNED_EXPORTERS=1` outside production.
- Visibility: the studios viewer rule AND the new setting **`cyrus_model_editor_enabled` (default OFF)**: everything 404s while it is off. Devhost: `CYRUS_MODEL_EDITOR_DEV=1` (ignored in production).

### 4. UI (`components/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/`, page `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/model-editor[?model=<key>]`)
Outliner (tree, hide/lock, drag to reparent, copy/mirror/group/delete), budgets, model bar (undo/redo, unsaved count, Save revision), draft and AI-candidate bars (Compare, Apply part with per-change checkboxes and per-overlap "Take Cyrus's", Apply, Reject), viewport (select/move/rotate/resize/pivot tools, Q/W/E/R/P, X mirror, Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z, Ctrl D, Del, H, Space; snap + angle snap; Persp/Front/Side; bones + wire toggles; muted X/Y/Z gizmo), pose timeline (clips, scrub, play/loop, key diamonds, drag to move a key, Key button), inspector (bone pivot/rotation/tag, cube from/size/inflate/material/shade, editor-only cube rotation/pivot with the RigSpec warning, the UV box sheet with drag-to-pin), Keyframe tab, Checks tab, prompt dock (UI only: without the dev fake it says "not connected yet, nothing was sent"). Dark + light via the shared tokens. Under 760 px: read-only turntable, "What changed" (incl. a restored draft), budgets, Reject / Approve revision (approve = save; disabled for plans that may not edit). Plans that may not edit get the same page read-only (viewing is never gated).
Viewport: `viewport-adapter.ts` (`ModelViewport` interface + `canvasViewport`, flat palette shading, no textures). The layer-1 three.js viewport should implement the same interface.

### 5. Tests and runs
- RAN: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-editor.test.ts` (61 tests: round trips for 3 fixtures with byte-identical `.bbmodel` + skin, fixed point, every op incl. refusals, op-log replay, validation codes, UV == compiler, sampler/matrices == compiler/preview, scene picking, merge cases, gate matrix, autosave, exporters + Hytale golden, save path with an in-memory store, HTTP flag-off 404, client import graph has no `node:`).
- RAN: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-timeline.test.ts` (9 tests). Full suite after merging the latest `feature/cyrus-r2`: `devhost test test/cyrus-*.test.ts test/modbuilder-*.test.ts` 1706/1707 pass; the one failure is `test/cyrus-admin.test.ts` exiting at process level under the loaded parallel run (no subtest failed; it passes alone 31/31; nothing here touches it). `devhost tsc` clean.
- RAN on devhost (throwaway DB, `scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` + `scripts/cyrus/model-editor-fixtures.ts`, env `CYRUS_MODEL_EDITOR_DEV=1 CYRUS_MODEL_EDITOR_DRAFTS=memory`, `test/e2e/cyrus-model-editor.shots.mjs`): 8 screenshots `editor-*.png` in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/` (dark, light, AI candidate with 1 overlap, checks with a refused cube rotation, keyframe tab + clip event after a REAL "Saved as revision 9" through the API, Saka view-only, phone dark/light reviewing a real autosaved server draft).
- NOT RUN: no real Minecraft client load of an editor-saved creature (the compiler output is byte-identical to the build path, which was loaded on Paper 26.2 in R3); nothing Hytale has been loaded by a Hytale client; no production DB, no migration.

### 6. Known gaps / next
- The next build of a mod regenerates its creature row (origin `generated`) and would win over an editor row; the asset sync needs the same "keep studio edits" rule textures have (`currentStudioDoc`).
- RigSpec v1.1 + rig-c2 (plan F2): cube ids, UV pins, cube rotation in the shipped format; until then those are editor-only and validated as such.
- `CyrusModelDraft` table (F1) for server drafts; ItemCuboidSpec (F3) for 3D items is not in this editor yet (creatures only).
- AI edits: the candidate + merge UI is wired to the deterministic fake only; the real backend (a change build returning a RigSpec) is not built.

## Cyrus motion core (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r21-motion`, NOT deployed, behind `CYRUS_DESIGNER` (off))

Owner decision: motion, animation and effects are foundational and game-neutral. Plan: `docs/cyrus/motion/MOTION-PLAN.md` (copy of `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v4-motion/MOTION-PLAN.md`); research `cyrus-research/R-motion-effects.md`.

**Core (`lib/cyrus/motion/`, pure, client-safe, no game code, no Nxeon imports).**
- `spec.ts`: **MotionSpec v1** (Zod; JSON Schema `motion.v1.schema.json` generated by `scripts/cyrus/build-motion-artifacts.ts`, stale-checked by the test). Units: 1 = one block, degrees Euler Z*Y*X about the node pivot, integer ticks at 20 Hz. Rig nodes `bone | part | socket | hinge{axis,min,max} | wheel{axle,radius,steer} | seat | emitter` with an optional preview `proxy` box. Clips (`once | loop | hold | pingpong`) with five track kinds: `transform` (keys or a wave), `particle` (inline emitters, seeded), `sound` (`sound:<library id>` or a namespaced key), `material` (emissive / opacity / tint / frame / brightness), `event` (optional `attach` / `detach` of `$actor` to a seat: vehicles are expressible, not built). Machines: integer vars, states (clip, `onEnter` set/add/emit, `after`), guarded transitions with `minTicks`.
- `sample.ts`: `sample(spec, clip, tick)` (pure, 1e-4 rounded), `cues(clip, from, to]` (no double fire, loop / pingpong aware), `particleBirths` / `particlesAt` (analytic, seeded mulberry32; every game lowering spawns exactly these births).
- `machine.ts`: `MachineRunner` / `runMachine` (after, then inputs, then emits; max 8 transitions per tick).
- `simulate.ts`: frames (state, clip tick, cues, pose, particles) + `eventLog`.
- `validate.ts`: `validateMotion(spec, capability)` -> structured issues `{path, code, severity, message}`: schema, rig (one root, cycles, hinge axis / limits, wheel axle), timing (key order, cue after end, `after` on a looping clip, zero-tick cycles), machine refs, reachability, and the capability's caps (nodes, depth, clips, tracks, keys, duration, particles per tick / per play, sounds, machines, states, transitions, entities per instance).

Phones: read-only turntable, what changed in the autosaved draft, what ships, Approve (saves the draft) / Reject (drops it). Autosave 5 s after the last edit.

# AA: Model Studio integration + layer 3 (r30, 2026-10-11)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r30-modelstudio` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r30`), from `feature/cyrus-r2` 3969bee6d3, latest r2 merged in. NOT merged into r2, NOT deployed, no migration run, no flag flipped. The layer-3 UI follows the v3 retexture mockup, which the owner has NOT reviewed. Docs: DOCUMENTATION.md "Cyrus Model Studio: integration seams (r30)" and "layer 3, mesh retexture + light edit". Owner items: OWNER-ACTIONS.md "Model Studio integration + layer 3".

## Commits (in order)
1. **1a viewport/camera/clock**: the cuboid editor draws through the layer-1 three.js `ModelViewport` (2D canvas only as no-WebGL fallback); EditorScene -> shared `ModelScene`; one orbit camera (`CAM_PRESETS`, `fitOrbit`, `projectOrbit` = inverse of `rayFromOrbit`); editor picking uses the same ray maths; `PlaybackClock` is a holder around the timeline clock (one clock).
2. **1b editor saves survive builds**: one current-creature rule (`creature-state.ts`) for both studios and the build sync; the sync 3-way merges the build's RigSpec INTO a current editor save with the existing editor merge (human wins), ships the merged creature, marks the build row `studioKept`. `CyrusModelDraft.surface` (paint/editor/mesh) + manual SQL `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-11-cyrus-model-drafts.sql` (NOT applied). Editor drafts wired to it. Fixed a manifest-path collision between the paint doc and the editor doc.
3. **1c creature paint -> delivered skin**: `creature/paint.ts` + a compile hook; paint stored in `MbAssets.creatures[].paint`, delivery re-compiles and proves the bytes.
4. **1d handgun grip (PROPOSED, OFF)**: `gripOnFist` behind `CYRUS_HANDGUN_GRIP_FIX`; off = byte-identical (golden + proved equal to the previous code); on = grip distance 1.948 -> 0 (third person), 3.148 -> 0 (first person).
5. **2 layer 3**: MeshEditDoc v1, the one op log (`oplog.ts`, editor history now uses it), part transforms on named parts with snapping and limits, per-channel lossless layers + UV island fills, template sliders validated by the meshgen schema + deterministic block-out + rebuild (0 tokens), legal badge from the ledger (moved to client-safe `assets3d/ledger.ts`), export picker from asset profiles, plan gate (All models, server side, fail closed), drafts, phone approve. Page `/dashboard/cyrus/<build>/studio/mesh`.
6. Docs, owner actions, tracker, this report.

## RAN
- `devhost tsc`: clean (after each step and after the r2 merge).
- Tests (node-2): new `test/cyrus-modelstudio-integration.test.ts` (merge rule, sync kept/merged/no-base, drafts surface, paint compile + delivery proof + size mismatch), `test/cyrus-handgun-grip.test.ts` (goldens), `test/cyrus-modelstudio-layer3.test.ts` on two REAL meshgen glbs (doc, ops, op log replay, sliders, block-out, export honesty, legal rules, part maths, server gate/stale/retention/rebuild/drafts, HTTP, client import graph has no `node:`). Full Cyrus suite after the r2 merge: see the final numbers line below.
- REAL Test Flight (node-2, lock, torn down): Paper 26.2 + BetterModel 3.5.0, a painted banshee head (294 texels): the delivered `.bbmodel` equals the compile, spawn/despawn pass, and BetterModel's own `build.zip` holds `textures/item/a.png` **byte-identical to the painted PNG**. `creature-paint-r30-flight-2026-10-11.json`.
- Devhost UI runs with screenshots I looked at and fixed (layout, overlap count, block-out colours, slider undo steps): `impl-shots/r30-editor-threeviewport-*.png` (editor on three.js, dark/light/phone) and `impl-shots/layer3-*.png` (dark, light, block-out sliders + rebuild 503, a REAL save through the UI = revision 11 reopened, game-derived, Saka locked, phone dark/light approving a real autosaved draft).

## NOT RUN / not built
- No game client looked at anything (painted skins, grip fix, meshes).
